subject: Control/Data Contracts & Acceptance Matrix — Vertex Private VPC
messages:
From: Jill Park <jill.park@vertexsys.com>

Subject: Vertex private VPC — acceptance checklist and initial diagrams

Hi team,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. Attached are the network drawings we referenced — simplified public/private subnets and our transit/peering zones. Before we lock the timeline for the on‑prem attachment, we need a concrete "acceptance matrix" from Redwood that spells out the control‑plane/data‑plane contracts (ports, TLS expectations, auth, logging/retention), acceptable egress patterns, and the items your ops team will validate during the handoff.

High level asks from our side:
- Clear list of ports and protocols required between customer edge and Redwood control endpoints (DNS names/IP ranges).
- Expected mTLS/cert flow and KMS/HSM integration points for keys.
- Audit/log retention SLOs and what evidence will be provided.
- Any required NAT/eip mappings, and whether we should provide a private NAT or let Redwood manage egress.

Can you provide a draft by Thu so we can attach it to our internal change request? I can bring Peter (networking) on the call if helpful.

Attachments: vertex-network-drawings.pdf (diagram stub)

Thanks,
Jill Park
Director, SRE — Vertex Systems
jill.park@vertexsys.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Vertex private VPC — acceptance checklist and initial diagrams

Jill — thanks, this is helpful. Putting a draft acceptance matrix below (high level) so your team can review. I've attached a spreadsheet with rows we will use during ops validation.

Draft acceptance matrix (summary):
1) Control-plane endpoints
   - Hosts: control.redwood-inference.com (regional) — will provide ASN + IP ranges 72h before cutover
   - Ports: 443 (HTTPS) for API/agent registration; 5222 if using the legacy agent tunnel (opt-in)
   - TLS: mutual TLS required for agent registration + API calls. Redwood CA issued certs by default; we support customer-supplied certs via KMS/HSM provisioning.
2) Data-plane (inference node)
   - Egress: outbound to model artifact storage (S3 endpoints) and telemetry collectors. Typical ports 443, 80 (artifact redirects).
   - Ingress: customer traffic stays in-customer VPC; Redwood nodes will be deployed in a peered subnet. We require no direct inbound from public internet to nodes.
3) Service mesh / demarcation
   - We recommend a local sidecar (Envoy) controlled by Redwood-provided config; control plane talks to sidecars over mTLS on port 15010 (example).
4) Audit/logging
   - Telemetry: tokenized traces and metrics pushed to customer collector endpoint over HTTPS.
   - Retention: operational logs retained 90 days by default; can be extended. Evidence: daily log export link + filtered audit log export for acceptance tests.
5) KMS/HSM
   - Integration: support for AWS KMS and external HSM via PKCS#11 bridge. Customer must provide key policy allowing Redwood service principal to sign/unwrap during initial onboarding.
6) NAT & egress
   - Two modes: customer‑managed NAT (preferred for regulated data) or Redwood-managed NAT with provided egress IP ranges. Confirm which you prefer.

Next actions:
- I attached the "redwood-vpc-acceptance-matrix.xlsx" with the above expanded into testable rows.
- Please confirm whether Vertex will provide the NAT and the KMS/HSM details.
- Propose a short runbook walkthrough session (30m) next Tue/Wed.

Attachment: redwood-vpc-acceptance-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — this is exactly the level we needed. A couple clarifying Qs before we run it through change control:
- For control.redwood-inference.com, can you commit to an IP range and announcement window? Our firewall rules require a list of CIDRs, not hostnames.
- For the mTLS flow: does Redwood expect us to rotate certs on our side or can Redwood handle rotation for customer-provided certs? What is the recommended lifespan?
- On KMS: we prefer to present a customer HSM. What specific PKCS#11 endpoints do you require?

Also: our compliance team flagged that audit exports need to be verifiable (signed). Can Redwood provide a signed export or a checksum for daily export files?

I'll bring Peter on the call if we need network-level walk-throughs.

Jill

Jill/Peter — quick technical notes to answer the items above and reduce back-and-forth: 

1) Control-plane IPs
   - We will provide the final /22 CIDR block for the regional control endpoint at least 72 hours before cutover. For acceptance testing you can temporarily open the hostname (control.redwood-inference.com) + the announced CIDRs.
2) Cert rotation
   - If you provide certs (customer-supplied), Redwood can coordinate rotation via the KMS/HSM integration; recommended TTL 90 days for leaf certs and automatic rotation every 60 days for intermediate keys.
3) PKCS#11/HSM details
   - Standard PKCS#11 2.40 interface; we use an HSM agent that expects slot/token label + module path. We'll share sample config after NDA.
4) Signed audit exports
   - We can produce daily gzipped exports with an SHA256 checksum signed by Redwood's signing key. That meets most compliance requirements; we can add an Intel-signed timestamp on request.
5) NAT & egress options
   - If Vertex elects customer-managed NAT, ensure we have NAT mappings for the model artifact S3 endpoints and telemetry collectors. If Redwood manages NAT, we will allocate a small pool of egress IPs and publish them to your firewall.

I've sketched a recommended demarc pattern (attached) showing service mesh sidecars inside the customer subnet, a control-channel tunnel to Redwood control-plane endpoints, and local telemetry forwarders to your collector.

Attachment: control-data-demarc-sketch.png (image stub)

— Grace
